'''Daniel K. Riskin''' (born January 1, 1975) is a Canadian [[evolutionary biologist]], [[television personality]] and [[Television producer|producer]]. He hosted the Canadian television series ''[[Daily Planet (TV series)|Daily Planet]]''.

==Early life and education==
He was born and raised in [[Edmonton]], [[Alberta]] and currently lives in [[Toronto]], [[Ontario]]. He received a [[BSc]] in [[zoology]] from the [[University of Alberta]], an [[MSc]] in [[biology]] from [[York University]], and a [[PhD]] in zoology from [[Cornell University]]. He also completed post-doctoral studies at [[Boston University]] and [[Brown University]].<ref name="My Science Research">{{cite web |url=http://www.noctilio.com/my-science-research/ |title=My Science Research |work=Noctilio |accessdate=July 21, 2014 |author=Riskin, Daniel K. |archive-date=July 28, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140728193829/http://www.noctilio.com/my-science-research/ |url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Career==

===Science===
During high school, Riskin read a book called ''Just Bats'' by M. Brock Fenton. The book inspired him, so he contacted Fenton, then a professor at York University, and told him that he would like to meet him. Fenton invited him to come out to join his lab. Within a few months, Riskin was catching bats in [[Costa Rica]].<ref name="Globe and Mail">{{cite news |url=https://www.theglobeandmail.com/arts/television/a-good-time-to-be-a-geek-and-to-be-daily-planets-dan-riskin/article590557/ |title=A good time to be a geek, and to be Daily Planet's Dan Riskin |publisher=Phillip Crawley |work=The Globe and Mail |date=August 15, 2011 |accessdate=July 21, 2014 |author=Ryan, Andrew}}</ref>

Riskin has studied bats in [[Costa Rica]], United States, Canada, [[Anguilla]], France, Israel, Australia, New Zealand, [[Trinidad]], [[Ecuador]], [[South Africa]] and [[Madagascar]] and has filmed in United States, [[Morocco]], England, China and Germany.{{citation needed|date=July 2014}} He has authored or co-authored more than 20 papers.<ref name="My Science Research" />

After publishing a scientific paper about running vampire bats in 2005, Riskin was interviewed on Discovery Canada's flagship daily science show, ''[[Daily Planet (TV series)|Daily Planet]]'', by then-host [[Natasha Stillwell]]. Years later, Riskin joined the show as the replacement for long-time host [[Jay Ingram]].<ref name="Globe and Mail" />

===Television===
Riskin appears on the [[Animal Planet]] series ''[[Monsters Inside Me]]'', which is about parasites, as an expert.<ref name="Monsters Inside Me Press Kit">{{cite web |url=http://press.discovery.com/ekits/monsters-inside-me-2/template.cfm?page=dan-raskin-bio |title=Dan Riskin Bio |publisher=Discovery Channel |work=Monsters Inside Me Season 2 – Animal Planet – Press Kit |accessdate=July 21, 2014 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20140726115420/http://press.discovery.com/ekits/monsters-inside-me-2/template.cfm?page=dan-raskin-bio |archivedate=July 26, 2014 |df=mdy}}</ref>

To promote that show, Riskin has appeared on ''[[The Dr. Oz Show]]'' (2009), ''[[The Tonight Show with Jay Leno]]'' (2010), and several times on ''[[The Late Late Show with Craig Ferguson]]'' (2010–2014).<ref name="Globe and Mail" /> Riskin has also appeared on the shows ''[[Evolve (TV series)|Evolve]]'' (2008) and ''Bedbug Apocalypse'' (2011). In 2010, Riskin became the co-host of ''[[Daily Planet (TV series)|Daily Planet]]'', on [[Discovery Channel (Canada)|Discovery Channel Canada]] with [[Ziya Tong]].<ref name="CV">{{cite web |url=https://www.noctilio.com/pdfs/riskin_cv.pdf |title=Daniel K. Riskin – Curriculum Vitae |date=May 29, 2014 |accessdate=July 21, 2014 |author=Riskin, Daniel K. |pages=3–4}}</ref>

Although Riskin now works full-time in television, he still dabbles in bat research. On one of his first segments on ''Daily Planet'', he filmed in China to look for the fishing bat which catches fish with its feet.<ref name="York">{{cite web |url=http://alumni.news.yorku.ca/2011/11/01/york-grad-conquers-daily-planet/ |title=York grad lands on 'Daily Planet' |publisher=York University |date=November 1, 2011 |accessdate=July 21, 2014}}</ref>

===Writing===
Riskin's first book, ''Mother Nature is Trying to Kill You: A Lively Tour Through the Dark Side of the Natural World'', was published by [[Touchstone Books]] on March 4, 2014.<ref name="Mother Nature">{{cite book |url=https://archive.org/details/mothernatureistr0000risk |title=Mother Nature is Trying to Kill You: A Lively Tour Through the Dark Side of the Natural World |publisher=Touchstone Books |author=Riskin, Dan |year=2014 |location=New York |isbn=978-1476707549 |url-access=registration}}</ref> Riskin also published a children's book in 2022 titled, "Fiona the Fruit Bat" about a short-tailed fruit bat who is afraid of the dark but has to make a leap of faith to take her first flight. Beautifully illustrated by Rachel Qiuqi.<ref>Published by Greystone Books https://greystonebooks.com/products/fiona-the-fruit-bat?srsltid=AfmBOoqobzVt36cDn0A1fYw4eNuLNgnPVvf69NaC6gp3qvTSktYra95A</ref>

== Podcast Host ==
* '' Inside the Breakthrough - How Science Comes to Life '' - Host (2021-2022)
Sponsored by Canadian company SciMar, the podcast captivatingly details stories about science and how their lessons can be applied to scientific breakthroughs today. All episodes conclude with how the Canadian company SciMar utilizes these themes to push forward research into type 2 diabetes through shifting the paradigm from investigating the pancreas to the liver through the protein hepatilin (or HISS- Hepatic insulin sensitizing substance). <ref>{{cite web |url=https://insidethebreakthrough.com/}}</ref>
